_comment: Expected anonymous-access surface of the Supabase database, measured against
production on 2026-08-18 after the RLS remediation. This is the mirror that
CLAUDE.md's backup law asks for: RLS policy state is configuration living in one
mutable place, and until now it was recorded nowhere.
It records ACCESS CLASS, not row counts. Counts change as the club adds events and
classes; access class should never change without someone deciding it should.
denied  - anon must read ZERO rows. Any row here is a regression.
public  - anon may read rows. Deliberate, reviewed, non-sensitive.
Refresh procedure and the meaning of each field: security/README.md.
source_of_truth: live probe with the published anon key; see security/2026-08-18-supabase-rls-exposure.pdf section 5

public_rationale.central_classes: Policy gates on visibility=public AND status in (scheduled,in_progress). Published class listings.
public_rationale.central_clubs: Policy 'Anon can read clubs by slug' but qual=true, so it returns all 3 clubs. Non-sensitive. Name/definition mismatch noted in the audit record section 5.
public_rationale.central_events: Policy gates on status=published AND visibility=public. Public event listings.
public_rationale.central_form_definitions: Anon can read form_definitions, qual=true. Form schemas the public forms need to render.
public_rationale.central_option_lists: anon_select_option_lists, qual=true. Dropdown option data for public forms.
public_rationale.central_organizations: Anon can read organizations, qual=true. Non-sensitive.

tour_bookings::Anon can insert bookings.note: Grants INSERT with no USING clause, so it cannot read or destroy. Audit record section 8.3 proved the booking flow does not need it: book-tour writes as service_role. Retained during remediation so the fix could not break bookings under any hypothesis. Safe to drop.
